instruction:
Use Internet Archive Help Center pages to build a retrieval guide for five needs: a title-and-creator metadata match, a phrase somewhere inside digitized books, a phrase within one already identified book, words in television captions, and an older version of a known website URL. For each identify the correct search mode, what its index contains and one documented limitation. Read Search - A Basic Guide, Search - Building Powerful, Complex Queries, Search - Tips & Troubleshooting, Using the Wayback Machine, Wayback Machine General Information and the FAQ on publishers blocking the Wayback Machine. Construct, as answer text only, a metadata query for items whose title contains the exact phrase lunar atlas, whose creator contains Rivera, and whose publication date is from 1900 through 1950 inclusive; then give a variant excluding subject fiction. Explain whether the same Boolean/field syntax is documented for full-text search. Give a checklist for detecting that a followed archived link has changed capture date or reached the live web, and reconcile any apparent conflict between older general help and newer blocking guidance by citing and labelling their scope rather than guessing. Do not save/archive pages, borrow items or submit a removal request.

Stopping condition: Stop when the five-mode guide, two query strings, syntax-scope explanation and archive-date/live-web/coverage checklist are supported by the six named help pages, with any documentation conflict explicitly identified.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Identify the correct search mode, what its index contains, and one documented limitation for finding a title-and-creator metadata match. Full credit for providing all three elements based on the specified help pages, OR if the required help pages are unavailable and the agent clearly reports this limitation. Partial credit if only 1-2 elements are provided. Support the retrieval guide, queries and checklist with source URLs from the six help pages named in the task.

Identify the correct search mode, what its index contains, and one documented limitation for finding a phrase somewhere inside digitized books. Full credit for providing all three elements, OR reporting if the source help pages are inaccessible. Partial credit if only 1-2 elements are provided.

items.criterion: Guide - Phrase within one identified book
items.description: Identify the correct search mode, what its index contains, and one documented limitation for finding a phrase within one already identified book. Full credit for providing all three elements, OR reporting if the source help pages are inaccessible. Partial credit if only 1-2 elements are provided.

Identify the correct search mode, what its index contains, and one documented limitation for finding words in television captions. Full credit for providing all three elements, OR reporting if the source help pages are inaccessible. Partial credit if only 1-2 elements are provided.

items.criterion: Guide - Older version of a known website URL
items.description: Identify the correct search mode, what its index contains, and one documented limitation for finding an older version of a known website URL using the Wayback Machine. Full credit for providing all three elements, OR reporting if the source help pages are inaccessible. Partial credit if only 1-2 elements are provided.

Construct, as answer text only, a metadata query for items whose title contains the exact phrase 'lunar atlas', whose creator contains 'Rivera', and whose publication date is from 1900 through 1950 inclusive. Full credit for a properly formatted query according to the help pages, OR reporting if the query building pages are unavailable. Partial credit if the query contains minor syntax errors but attempts to satisfy all constraints.

items.criterion: Construct variant metadata query excluding fiction
items.description: Construct a variant of the base query that explicitly excludes the subject 'fiction'. Full credit for successfully applying the exclusion syntax, OR reporting if the help documentation is unavailable. Partial credit for incorrect syntax that still attempts exclusion.

Explain whether the same Boolean/field syntax used for metadata applies to full-text search, based on the documented help pages. Full credit for an accurate explanation derived from the documentation, OR reporting if the documentation is down.

Provide a checklist for detecting that a followed archived link has changed capture date or reached the live web. Full credit for identifying clear indicators from the help pages, OR reporting if the pages are unavailable.

Reconcile any apparent conflict between older general help and newer blocking guidance by citing and labelling their scope. Full credit for explicitly identifying the conflict and explaining the scope of each based on the text, OR reporting if the pages cannot be loaded. No credit if the agent guesses without citing the text.

items.criterion: Adhere to read-only and negative constraints
items.description: Ensure the agent did not save/archive pages, borrow items, submit a removal request, or use unauthorized external programs/APIs. Full credit if all negative constraints are respected. Zero credit if any unauthorized action is taken.
